surprises.description: Invesco’s adjusted operating margin reached 40.7%, well above the preview’s 37.5%–38.5% base-case range and the 37.5% Q2 baseline. The increase was more than 3 percentage points sequentially, rather than just a gradual move toward the high 30s.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating margin expanded to 40.7%,” up “more than 3 percentage points sequentially and 650 basis points year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted operating margin vs. 37.5% baseline”; the base case expected “37.5–38.5%,” while management was focused on “pushing into the high 30s.”

surprises.description: Net revenue yield was 21.5 bps, below the approximately 22.07 bps implied by consensus and a larger compression than the roughly 0.4 bps already baked into expectations. Management attributed pressure to money-market and ETF mix as well as Canadian sales.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net revenue yield declined to 21.5 basis points (exit yield 21.3 bps),” pressured “about 0.7 bps by mix shift toward money market funds and ETFs and 0.2 bps from Canadian sales.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus $1.385B on $2,510.2B average AUM implies 22.07bps — about 0.4bp of compression baked in.”

surprises.description: Invesco had already repurchased another $1.5 billion of MassMutual preferred stock, leaving $1 billion outstanding. The preview expected the remaining $3 billion repurchase later in the year or early next year, conditional on revolver paydown, so this was earlier and substantially further along than anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Repurchased an additional $1.5 billion of MassMutual preferred stock,” bringing repurchases to “$3 billion over 18 months and leaving just $1 billion outstanding.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “$3B remaining MassMutual preferred” was expected “later this year or early next year,” contingent on “finishing the revolver paydown.”

surprises.description: Adjusted diluted EPS was $0.72, below the $0.74 consensus and the preview’s $0.76–$0.78 base case, despite the sharp margin expansion and higher adjusted operating income.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus adjusted diluted EPS was “$0.74”; the preview’s base case was “$0.76–0.78.”

surprises.description: Despite the preview’s concern about lower-priced Nasdaq-100 competition, QQQ products collectively attracted $16 billion of net inflows, alongside nearly $29 billion of ETF and index inflows and record ETF and index AUM.
surprises.fact_evidence: “ETF and index AUM reached a record $775 billion with nearly $29 billion of net inflows,” while “QQQ products collectively drew $16 billion in net inflows.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted competition from BlackRock and State Street selling Nasdaq-100 exposure at “0.10% against QQQ’s 0.18%” and described QQQ’s competitive position as a key issue.
